title: Half of US Workers Thinking About a Backup Career
paragraphs: Many American workers are not planning to leave their jobs right now. But a large number of them are quietly preparing a "plan B," according to a new survey.

The survey was carried out by Talker Research for TripleTen, a company that offers online courses in technology skills. It asked 2,000 full-time workers in the US about their career plans in September.

The results showed that 48% of workers are "career cushioning." This means they are exploring other career options while they stay in their current jobs. It is a way for people to protect themselves in case something happens to their job. Of the people who are career cushioning, 77% said they have already started preparing for a backup career.

Young workers were the most likely to have a plan B. Around 59% of Gen Z workers said they had thought about a backup career. The number was 54% for millennials, 40% for Gen X and only 22% for baby boomers.

Jobs in technology were the most popular choice for a backup career. Most people also believe that what they have learned at work will help them. In fact, 83% said the skills from their current job would be useful in their backup career.

Other surveys show that many American workers are thinking about change. For example, a survey by the recruitment company Robert Half found that 46% of US professionals planned to look for a new job in the second half of 2026.
That number was much higher than before. In the first half of 2026, it was 38%, and one year earlier, it was only 27%.
